# Lab 07 — Audit Logging & Monitoring

**Objective:** Review the audit log trail generated by all actions in Labs 01–06, verify that changes are recorded, and understand how to filter and interpret log entries.

**Time:** 15–20 minutes  
**Difficulty:** Beginner–Intermediate  
**Cost:** Free

---

## Before You Start

Ensure you have completed Labs 01–06. The value of this lab depends on the volume of events recorded in previous steps — the more actions you took, the richer the log to review.

---

## Background

Every action taken in Entra ID — creating a user, adding a group member, assigning a role, disabling an account — is automatically recorded in the **Audit Log**. This is not optional or configurable: it is always on and tamper-evident.

The audit log is your proof of compliance and your primary tool for security investigations. **Sign-in Logs** record every authentication attempt. In a lab environment, sign-in logs will be sparse because the test users are not actively logging in. In production, sign-in logs detect suspicious authentication patterns — failed attempts, logins from unusual locations, and impossible travel scenarios.

---

## Steps

### 1. Navigate to Audit Logs

1. In the Azure Portal, navigate to **Microsoft Entra ID**.
2. In the left sidebar under **Monitoring**, select **Audit logs**.

> **Expected result:** A list of audit log entries appears. Each entry shows: Date, Service, Category, Activity, Status, Target(s), and Initiated by (Actor).

---

### 2. Review the Log Overview

Scroll through recent entries. You should see events corresponding to actions in previous labs:

| Lab action | Audit log activity |
|---|---|
| User created (Lab 02) | "Add user" |
| Group created (Lab 03) | "Add group" |
| Member added to group (Lab 03) | "Add member to group" |
| Role assigned (Lab 04) | "Add member to role" |
| Application created (Lab 05) | "Add application" |
| User assigned to app (Lab 05) | "Add app role assignment to user" |
| User profile updated (Lab 06) | "Update user" |
| Member removed from group (Lab 06) | "Remove member from group" |
| Account disabled (Lab 06) | "Update user" (with accountEnabled → false in modified properties) |

> **Expected result:** Multiple log entries corresponding to the above activities are visible. If the list appears empty, check the date filter — ensure it covers today's date. Click **Add filters** → **Date** to adjust.

---

### 3. Filter by Target User

Trace all activity related to **John Smith**:

1. Click **Add filters** above the log list.
2. Select **Target** from the filter options.
3. Enter **John Smith** and apply.

> **Expected result:** The filtered log shows all actions where John Smith was the target — his creation, group assignments, profile update, group removal, and application reassignment. This is the complete lifecycle trace for one identity, from Joiner through Mover.

---

### 4. Examine a Single Log Entry in Detail

1. Click on a **"Update user"** entry (e.g., John Smith's department change).
2. Review the detail panel:

| Field | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| **Activity** | What happened |
| **Initiated by (Actor)** | Who made the change |
| **Target(s)** | Which object was changed |
| **Modified properties** | Old value → New value |
| **Date** | When the change occurred |

> **Expected result:** The "Modified properties" section on John Smith's department update shows the old value (HR) and new value (Finance). This is what makes audit logs useful for investigations — not just that something changed, but what it changed from and to, and who made the change.

---

### 5. Review Sign-in Logs

1. In the left sidebar under **Monitoring**, select **Sign-in logs**.
2. Review any entries present.

> **Expected result:** In a lab environment, sign-in logs are sparse or empty for the test users (they were never actively logging in). Your own admin authentication activity may be visible. In production, this view shows every authentication attempt across all users in real time.

---

## IAM Concepts

**Compliance Logging** — Audit logs are automatic and tamper-evident. Every privileged action is recorded: who did it, what they did, and when. This is a baseline requirement for SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and most other compliance frameworks.

**Audit Traceability** — The ability to filter logs by user, time, activity type, or target means you can reconstruct the complete history of any identity — from creation through every access change to offboarding. This is essential for both scheduled compliance audits and unplanned security investigations.

**SIEM Integration (Production Context)** — In production, Entra ID audit and sign-in logs feed into a SIEM (e.g., Microsoft Sentinel). The SIEM applies detection rules to identify anomalies — impossible travel, brute-force attempts, access to unusual resources — and generates alerts. The audit log you have reviewed is the raw data that enables that intelligence layer.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Audit log is empty | Date filter set to a past or future range | Click the date filter and set to "Last 24 hours" or "Last 7 days" |
| Cannot find a specific event | Filter too narrow | Clear all filters and scroll manually, or search by activity keyword |
| "Modified properties" is blank on a log entry | Some activity types do not record property diffs | Look for "Update user" events specifically — these capture old/new values |
